capabilities: Run manual or scheduled incremental backups via rclone sync
Move overwritten or deleted files into timestamped folders instead of losing them
Locate rclone or install it via winget, brew, curl, or a verified download
Restore single files, the latest state, or an earlier state from timestamped folders
Exclude paths and delete incremental folders older than a set number of days
extras: Desktop only (needs Node.js and local executables, does not load on mobile); runs external programs (rclone, and winget/brew/curl only when installing); no telemetry and nothing sent during backups; the manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
intentEvidence: modelled on Simple Backup — same schedule, progress notice and wake-lock
motivation: The author built it for large vaults (10-100+ GB) where unchanged files should not be re-read or rewritten and media should not be re-compressed.
problem: Obsidian's built-in File recovery only keeps local snapshots, so large vaults lack scheduled, versioned backups written to a folder outside the vault.

relations.evidence: modelled on Simple Backup — same schedule, progress notice and wake-lock
the copying is done by rclone sync --backup-dir

summary: Incremental vault backup plugin that runs rclone sync to keep a full mirror plus timestamped folders of every changed or deleted file.
